name: Poptin
summary: Popups, forms and coupons with a drag-and-drop editor, exit-intent and cart triggers, A/B testing, 70-plus native integrations and an email-marketing side with campaigns, automations and segments. Metered on unique monthly visitors, counted once per browser per 30 days. The combined Emails & Poptins product publishes no price for its recommended tier at any of its eighteen contact bands.
best_for: sites that want popups, forms and coupons with a genuinely usable free tier and a cheap first paid rung — $20 a month for 10,000 visitors, unlimited popups and no Poptin branding — and that are happy to run the email side elsewhere
skip_if: you want the combined email-and-popup product, because the recommended tier publishes no price at any list size; you need a second administrator or an API key, which is a $95 tier rather than a $20 one; or your traffic is measured in views rather than unique visitors, where a view-metered competitor may cost less
honest_knock:
The plan Poptin recommends does not have a price on it. Choose Emails & Poptins, and the Growth card renders the word “/month” with nothing in front of it. That is not a slow-loading figure: the contact selector works perfectly beside it — move it and the allowance updates from 500 to 1,500 to 7,500 active contacts — while the amount stays absent at every one of the eighteen bands, and the Free card in the same row renders its $0 without trouble. We checked three bands and inspected the card itself; there is no amount element in it. So the page invites you to size your list and then declines to tell you what sizing it costs.

Switch to the popup-only product and everything is priced, which makes the omission stranger rather than more forgivable. It also means the honest advice depends on which door you came through: if you want the popups, this is a transparent, cheap tool; if you want the email marketing alongside them, the price is a conversation.

The free plan is thinner than the feature list suggests. It carries 1,000 visitors a month, which is real, but the in-app billing page marks three things with a cross rather than a tick: Unbranded, Manage accounts, and Manage users & API keys. So the free tier shows Poptin's own branding on your popups. That is normal for the category, but the pricing page lists those rows under Free without making the distinction obvious.

Branding is settled at the first paid rung, but team access is not. Basic at $20 and Pro at $47 both still carry a cross on Manage accounts and on Manage users & API keys. If you need more than one person administering this, or an API key, the tier is Agency at $95 — four and a half times the entry price for a permission rather than for volume.

And read the meter definition before you size yourself. A unique visitor is counted per browser, not per person: the same buyer on a phone and a laptop is two, and anyone who clears cookies becomes new again. Your real headroom is therefore lower than your analytics suggests.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month billed annually ($25 monthly), 10,000 visitors
pricing.notes:
(read 18 September 2026 in a live browser on poptin.com/pricing, in both product modes and both billing cycles, with the in-app billing page at app.popt.in checked alongside it) The page opens with a question — “What are you looking for?” — and the answer changes the whole ladder.

Pick Poptins, the popup product, and every tier carries a figure. Free is $0 forever with 1,000 unique visitors a month, one domain and unlimited poptins. Basic is $20 a month billed annually ($240 a year) or $25 billed monthly, for 10,000 visitors and one domain. Pro, marked Most Popular, is $47 annually ($564) or $59 monthly, for 50,000 visitors and four domains. Agency is $95 annually ($1,140) or $119 monthly, starting at 150,000 visitors with a dropdown that climbs through 300,000, 500,000, 750,000, one million and two million, plus unlimited domains and premium support. The stated 20% annual saving checks out at all three rungs: $60 off $300, $144 off $708 and $288 off $1,428.

Pick Emails & Poptins, the combined product, and the ladder loses its prices. Free is $0 for 250 active contacts, 500 emails and 1,000 visitors. Growth — the tier the page marks RECOMMENDED — shows the word “/month” and no amount at all, at any of the eighteen contact bands in the selector. Enterprise is quote-only in both modes.

The meter is unique monthly visitors, and their FAQ defines it: anyone who loads a page carrying the snippet in the last 30 days, counted once however many sessions or pages they open — unless they clear cookies or switch device or browser, in which case they count again.

free_plan_evidence: Free is $0 forever with 1,000 unique visitors a month, one domain and unlimited poptins.

compare_with.name: Hello Bar, Moosend
compare_with.why:
Hello Bar is the closest comparison we carry, and the unit is the whole story. From our own dossier (re-verified 3 September 2026) Hello Bar charges $29 a month billed annually for up to 50,000 popup VIEWS, $49 for 150,000 and $99 for 500,000, with the limit applied per website. Poptin charges $47 for 50,000 unique VISITORS and $95 for 150,000. On the headline numbers Hello Bar is cheaper at every rung — but a visitor who sees three popups is one visitor and three views, so the ladders only line up if your visitors each see a single popup. Past roughly 1.6 popups per visitor, Poptin's unit is the cheaper one at the same number. Work out which you are before comparing the prices.

The free tiers differ in kind rather than degree: Poptin gives 1,000 visitors every month, Hello Bar gives 5,000 views in total rather than per month. One is a small permanent allowance, the other a trial with no clock on it.

Moosend is the peer for the email half, and it does the thing Poptin does not: it prices by list size across 21 steps from 500 to a million contacts, quoted monthly, biannually or annually (re-verified 6 September 2026). Poptin's Emails & Poptins mode has the same shape — eighteen contact bands — and no number attached to any of them. If the combined product is what you are shopping for, that is the difference that decides it.
